Part 2

What to improve before the codebase grows

The stage layer is a good foundation: one config model, one set of stage APIs, tests per stage. The cost of growth sits below and around it. Items are ordered by how much they slow down the next feature. Every change below can keep old import paths alive with re-export shims, which keeps it within team rules 2, 4 and 8.

1

Group the flat src/core into feature packages

About 40 modules sit side by side, mixing the run framework (runner, run, tracker, results store) with science code (preprocessing, features, training, tuning). Nothing on disk tells a new person which files belong to which stage.

Target layout: core/run/, core/preprocessing/, core/clustering/, core/features/, core/training/, core/evaluation/ (holdout, partitions, folds), core/tuning/. Leave a one-line shim at each old path.

2

Make adding a stage a one-place change

Stages are wired by hand in STAGE_ORDER, STAGE_DEPENDENCIES, REQUIRED_ARTIFACTS, a special case in _dependencies, CLI subcommands, two notebook tiers and docs. The holdout stage shows the drift: it has a CLI command but no thin or full notebook, and the main docs do not mention it.

A small Stage protocol (name, depends_on, required_artifacts, settings_from_config, run) and a registry. The runner, the CLI and a notebook generator read the registry. A test fails when a registered stage has no notebook or doc section.

3

Split the oversized modules

model_report.py 8,737 lines, heat_vis.py 3,198, unit_report.py 3,062, feature_extraction.py 2,755, service/app.py 2,758, train.py 2,255. Files this size cause merge conflicts between the four or five people working on them and are hard to test piece by piece.

Split by section: for the model report, data loading, metrics tables, plots and HTML assembly. For feature extraction, one module per feature family behind a registry.

4

Fix the layer direction

src/visualization/model_report.py imports run internals (v2_pipeline_run, removal_audit) and legacy src/utils/data_utils, while stages import visualization. train.py still edits sys.path and falls back to from utils.model_utils.

Set one direction, config → datasets/io → algorithms → stages → interfaces, with reports reading only artifacts and the run manifest. Enforce it with import-linter in CI. Remove the sys.path hack.

5

Merge duplicated utilities and tuners

build_gcs_uri exists in both src/core/config/paths.py:73 and src/utils/gcs_utils.py:78. The three tuners, three tune scripts and three experiment YAMLs follow one pattern.

One GCS helper module. One generic tuner, with each model's search space in YAML and a single lucia_pipeline.py tune --model command.

6

Separate active code from dead or legacy code

Nothing in src/, scripts/ or active notebooks imports ensemble_decisions.py, feature_selection_stable.py or rebuild_prediction_tables.py. heat_vis.py and site_leading_features.py serve only frozen notebooks/gilad. eran_preprocess.py is reached only from tests. File names like Feature_Extraction_BB_June3_LUCIA.py do not follow PEP 8.

Confirm with each owner, then move to src/legacy/ or delete. Rename non-PEP 8 files with shims.

7

Turn one-off scripts into config

Four pin_* scripts each hard-code one dataset cut (for example pin_type2_batch1_drophuge2108ch17.py). The next cut means a fifth script.

One datasets pin --spec configs/datasets/<name>.yaml command. The YAML records which patients and channels are dropped and why.

8

Tidy configs, notebooks and dependencies

Experiments live in both configs/experiments/ and configs/pipeline/experiments/. Notebooks are organised by person, with .py scripts inside notebooks/gilad. Five requirements files and no pyproject.toml. Optuna is missing from the venv, so the tuning tests are skipped.

Configs by study (lucia550/, relive/, type1_61/). Notebooks by purpose (pipeline/, exploration/<topic>/, legacy/). A pyproject.toml with extras [pipeline], [tuning], [gpu], [dashboard] and a lock file.

9

Give the dashboard a written input contract

breath_v2_adapter.py (968 lines) reverse-engineers run folders. Team rule 2 forbids changing outputs, so the adapter is the only thing pinning the run layout.

Version the run manifest schema, have the dashboard read only the manifest, and add a contract test that builds a bundle from the e2e test run.

Part 3

What is in docs/

No document carries a version number, status or owner. The only versioning is git history, so the table uses it: the date a file was added, the date it last changed, how many commits touched it, and who changed it last.

Part 4

How documentation is done today

Works wellThe README points to a reading order. Guides are written for tasks and include real commands. Team rule 9 asks for docs in the same change. test_grid_clean_doc.py already checks a doc against code. The review tracker has a clear status vocabulary.
One flat folder, six kinds of documentGuides, reference, explanations, branch handoffs, a personal run log, a review tracker and slide decks sit together. A reader cannot tell which are maintained and which are snapshots.
No version, status or ownerNothing says which pipeline version or commit a doc describes, who owns it, or when it was last checked. Readers have to run git log to judge freshness.
Overlap causes driftThe 1,044-line architecture doc repeats the repo tree, config layers, run commands and failures that the user guide, quickstart and configuration reference also cover. When the holdout stage arrived, it went into a new file and none of the four core docs were updated.
Stale and contradictory factsNEW_VM_SETUP.md checks out lenny/new_pipe. Two docs point to gilad/PR38. The canonical-modules doc calls notebooks/gilad the production chain, while the README says it is frozen.
Inconsistent naming and binariesUPPER_CASE, lower_case and a filename with spaces. Two identical .pptx files. Slides are binary copies of Markdown docs and drift silently from them.
Part 5

Proposed documentation system

Sort every doc by the question it answers, using the four Diátaxis types, plus two folders for point-in-time records. Maintained docs describe the current code and are updated in the same PR. Records are dated, never edited after the fact, and are allowed to go stale.

Rules that keep it in order

  1. Front matter on every maintained doc: title, type, status (draft, current, superseded, archived), owner, last_reviewed, applies_to (pipeline version or commit). Records also carry date and branch.
  2. One home per fact. The repo tree lives in one reference page, config keys in one, commands in one. Other docs link and do not copy.
  3. Version the pipeline, not each doc. Tag releases (v2.1.0), write user-facing changes to CHANGELOG.md, and set applies_to on docs. Git keeps the history of each file.
  4. Naming: lowercase kebab-case, no spaces. Records start with an ISO date.
  5. Generate reference from code: config keys from the config model and validation_only.yaml, CLI help from argparse. A test fails when a config key or stage is not documented, extending what test_grid_clean_doc.py does today.
  6. CI checks: broken relative links, missing front matter, and a warning when last_reviewed is older than 90 days.
  7. PR template: one checkbox, "Docs updated or not needed", with the doc path.
  8. Slides are exports. Keep the Markdown as source, store decks on Drive, link them from the index.

Migration in three steps

  1. Quick fixes, one PR: delete the duplicate PR38.pptx, fix the branch names in NEW_VM_SETUP.md and the two gilad/PR38 notes, correct the production-chain line in the canonical-modules doc, add holdout to the README, user guide and configuration reference, and rename the file with spaces.
  2. Move and label: create the folders, git mv files so history follows them, add front matter and docs/README.md. Update links in README.md and .cursor/rules rule 9.
  3. De-duplicate and generate: shrink the architecture doc to explanation only, generate the config and CLI references, and add the doc-coverage test and link check to CI.

① Interfaces scripts/, notebooks/pipeline

Entry points a person uses to start work.

② Configuration src/core/config, configs/

Turns layered YAML into one validated, frozen ResolvedPipelineConfig.

③ Run orchestration src/core

Decides which stages run, records what they produced, and moves runs to and from GCS.

  • Stage planner and resume: pipeline_runner.py
  • Run directory and manifest: v2_pipeline_run.py

The stable contract. Each stage has Settings, settings_from_config, run_* and a Result.

  • preprocessing: load, cut, align, normalise, blip filter, overrides

  • features: extraction, TSF, mRMR/pool selection, blind split
  • training: Monte-Carlo validation draws, threshold, test
  • holdout: patient-disjoint holdouts or k-fold OOF
  • visualization, model_reports

The science. Grouped here by feature; on disk they sit in one folder.

  • Signal preparation: schema mapping, cutting, alignment, Gilad path vs GRID_CLEAN path, trigger detection, blips

Gets clinical data out of Cloud SQL into immutable GCS datasets and back into runs.

  • Dataset contract and manifest: columns, commit marker, checksums
  • GCS store: cache and download by dataset id

A separate deployable that reads published runs.

Part 2

What to improve before the codebase grows

The stage layer is a good foundation: one config model, one set of stage APIs, tests per stage. The cost of growth sits below and around it. Items are ordered by how much they slow down the next feature. Every change below can keep old import paths alive with re-export shims, which keeps it within team rules 2, 4 and 8.

1

Group the flat src/core into feature packages

About 40 modules sit side by side, mixing the run framework (runner, run, tracker, results store) with science code (preprocessing, features, training, tuning). Nothing on disk tells a new person which files belong to which stage.

Target layout: core/run/, core/preprocessing/, core/clustering/, core/features/, core/training/, core/evaluation/ (holdout, partitions, folds), core/tuning/. Leave a one-line shim at each old path.

2

Make adding a stage a one-place change

Stages are wired by hand in STAGE_ORDER, STAGE_DEPENDENCIES, REQUIRED_ARTIFACTS, a special case in _dependencies, CLI subcommands, two notebook tiers and docs. The holdout stage shows the drift: it has a CLI command but no thin or full notebook, and the main docs do not mention it.

A small Stage protocol (name, depends_on, required_artifacts, settings_from_config, run) and a registry. The runner, the CLI and a notebook generator read the registry. A test fails when a registered stage has no notebook or doc section.

3

Split the oversized modules

model_report.py 8,737 lines, heat_vis.py 3,198, unit_report.py 3,062, feature_extraction.py 2,755, service/app.py 2,758, train.py 2,255. Files this size cause merge conflicts between the four or five people working on them and are hard to test piece by piece.

Split by section: for the model report, data loading, metrics tables, plots and HTML assembly. For feature extraction, one module per feature family behind a registry.

4

Fix the layer direction

src/visualization/model_report.py imports run internals (v2_pipeline_run, removal_audit) and legacy src/utils/data_utils, while stages import visualization. train.py still edits sys.path and falls back to from utils.model_utils.

Set one direction, config → datasets/io → algorithms → stages → interfaces, with reports reading only artifacts and the run manifest. Enforce it with import-linter in CI. Remove the sys.path hack.

5

Merge duplicated utilities and tuners

build_gcs_uri exists in both src/core/config/paths.py:73 and src/utils/gcs_utils.py:78. The three tuners, three tune scripts and three experiment YAMLs follow one pattern.

One GCS helper module. One generic tuner, with each model's search space in YAML and a single lucia_pipeline.py tune --model command.

6

Separate active code from dead or legacy code

Nothing in src/, scripts/ or active notebooks imports ensemble_decisions.py, feature_selection_stable.py or rebuild_prediction_tables.py. heat_vis.py and site_leading_features.py serve only frozen notebooks/gilad. eran_preprocess.py is reached only from tests. File names like Feature_Extraction_BB_June3_LUCIA.py do not follow PEP 8.

Confirm with each owner, then move to src/legacy/ or delete. Rename non-PEP 8 files with shims.

7

Turn one-off scripts into config

Four pin_* scripts each hard-code one dataset cut (for example pin_type2_batch1_drophuge2108ch17.py). The next cut means a fifth script.

One datasets pin --spec configs/datasets/<name>.yaml command. The YAML records which patients and channels are dropped and why.

8

Tidy configs, notebooks and dependencies

Experiments live in both configs/experiments/ and configs/pipeline/experiments/. Notebooks are organised by person, with .py scripts inside notebooks/gilad. Five requirements files and no pyproject.toml. Optuna is missing from the venv, so the tuning tests are skipped.

Configs by study (lucia550/, relive/, type1_61/). Notebooks by purpose (pipeline/, exploration/<topic>/, legacy/). A pyproject.toml with extras [pipeline], [tuning], [gpu], [dashboard] and a lock file.

9

Give the dashboard a written input contract

breath_v2_adapter.py (968 lines) reverse-engineers run folders. Team rule 2 forbids changing outputs, so the adapter is the only thing pinning the run layout.

Version the run manifest schema, have the dashboard read only the manifest, and add a contract test that builds a bundle from the e2e test run.

Part 2

What to improve before the codebase grows

The stage layer is a good foundation: one config model, one set of stage APIs, tests per stage. The cost of growth sits below and around it. Items are ordered by how much they slow down the next feature. Every change below can keep old import paths alive with re-export shims, which keeps it within team rules 2, 4 and 8.

1

Group the flat src/core into feature packages

About 40 modules sit side by side, mixing the run framework (runner, run, tracker, results store) with science code (preprocessing, features, training, tuning). Nothing on disk tells a new person which files belong to which stage.

Target layout: core/run/, core/preprocessing/, core/clustering/, core/features/, core/training/, core/evaluation/ (holdout, partitions, folds), core/tuning/. Leave a one-line shim at each old path.

2

Make adding a stage a one-place change

Stages are wired by hand in STAGE_ORDER, STAGE_DEPENDENCIES, REQUIRED_ARTIFACTS, a special case in _dependencies, CLI subcommands, two notebook tiers and docs. The holdout stage shows the drift: it has a CLI command but no thin or full notebook, and the main docs do not mention it.

A small Stage protocol (name, depends_on, required_artifacts, settings_from_config, run) and a registry. The runner, the CLI and a notebook generator read the registry. A test fails when a registered stage has no notebook or doc section.

3

Split the oversized modules

model_report.py 8,737 lines, heat_vis.py 3,198, unit_report.py 3,062, feature_extraction.py 2,755, service/app.py 2,758, train.py 2,255. Files this size cause merge conflicts between the four or five people working on them and are hard to test piece by piece.

Split by section: for the model report, data loading, metrics tables, plots and HTML assembly. For feature extraction, one module per feature family behind a registry.

4

Fix the layer direction

src/visualization/model_report.py imports run internals (v2_pipeline_run, removal_audit) and legacy src/utils/data_utils, while stages import visualization. train.py still edits sys.path and falls back to from utils.model_utils.

Set one direction, config → datasets/io → algorithms → stages → interfaces, with reports reading only artifacts and the run manifest. Enforce it with import-linter in CI. Remove the sys.path hack.

5

Merge duplicated utilities and tuners

build_gcs_uri exists in both src/core/config/paths.py:73 and src/utils/gcs_utils.py:78. The three tuners, three tune scripts and three experiment YAMLs follow one pattern.

One GCS helper module. One generic tuner, with each model's search space in YAML and a single lucia_pipeline.py tune --model command.

6

Separate active code from dead or legacy code

Nothing in src/, scripts/ or active notebooks imports ensemble_decisions.py, feature_selection_stable.py or rebuild_prediction_tables.py. heat_vis.py and site_leading_features.py serve only frozen notebooks/gilad. eran_preprocess.py is reached only from tests. File names like Feature_Extraction_BB_June3_LUCIA.py do not follow PEP 8.

Confirm with each owner, then move to src/legacy/ or delete. Rename non-PEP 8 files with shims.

7

Turn one-off scripts into config

Four pin_* scripts each hard-code one dataset cut (for example pin_type2_batch1_drophuge2108ch17.py). The next cut means a fifth script.

One datasets pin --spec configs/datasets/<name>.yaml command. The YAML records which patients and channels are dropped and why.

8

Tidy configs, notebooks and dependencies

Experiments live in both configs/experiments/ and configs/pipeline/experiments/. Notebooks are organised by person, with .py scripts inside notebooks/gilad. Five requirements files and no pyproject.toml. Optuna is missing from the venv, so the tuning tests are skipped.

Configs by study (lucia550/, relive/, type1_61/). Notebooks by purpose (pipeline/, exploration/<topic>/, legacy/). A pyproject.toml with extras [pipeline], [tuning], [gpu], [dashboard] and a lock file.

9

Give the dashboard a written input contract

breath_v2_adapter.py (968 lines) reverse-engineers run folders. Team rule 2 forbids changing outputs, so the adapter is the only thing pinning the run layout.

Version the run manifest schema, have the dashboard read only the manifest, and add a contract test that builds a bundle from the e2e test run.

  1. Front matter on every maintained doc: title, type, status (draft, current, superseded, archived), owner, last_reviewed, applies_to (pipeline version or commit). Records also carry date and branch.
  2. One home per fact. The repo tree lives in one reference page, config keys in one, commands in one. Other docs link and do not copy.
  3. Version the pipeline, not each doc. Tag releases (v2.1.0), write user-facing changes to CHANGELOG.md, and set applies_to on docs. Git keeps the history of each file.
  4. Naming: lowercase kebab-case, no spaces. Records start with an ISO date.
  5. Generate reference from code: config keys from the config model and validation_only.yaml, CLI help from argparse. A test fails when a config key or stage is not documented, extending what test_grid_clean_doc.py does today.
  6. CI checks: broken relative links, missing front matter, and a warning when last_reviewed is older than 90 days.
  7. PR template: one checkbox, "Docs updated or not needed", with the doc path.
  8. Slides are exports. Keep the Markdown as source, store decks on Drive, link them from the index.

Migration in three steps

  1. Quick fixes, one PR: delete the duplicate PR38.pptx, fix the branch names in NEW_VM_SETUP.md and the two gilad/PR38 notes, correct the production-chain line in the canonical-modules doc, add holdout to the README, user guide and configuration reference, and rename the file with spaces.
  2. Move and label: create the folders, git mv files so history follows them, add front matter and docs/README.md. Update links in README.md and .cursor/rules rule 9.
  3. De-duplicate and generate: shrink the architecture doc to explanation only, generate the config and CLI references, and add the doc-coverage test and link check to CI.

How the breath-analysis model pipeline is put together, where it will hurt as it grows, what the docs/ folder holds, and a proposed way to organise the documentation.

Blocks and their components

① Interfaces scripts/, notebooks/pipeline

Entry points a person uses to start work.

  • Headless CLI lucia_pipeline.py: run, stage, holdout, publish-results, publish-model(s), runs list/pull
  • Thin notebooks 01–06: one stage per notebook, no logic
  • Full notebooks: same stages plus read-only diagnostics and a partition audit
  • Ops scripts: hyperparameter tuning, dataset pinning, dataset publishing, run deletion, parity check, VM and GPU acceptance

② Configuration src/core/config, configs/

Turns layered YAML into one validated, frozen ResolvedPipelineConfig.

  • Layering: validation_only.yaml → run YAML → --set overrides
  • Validation (validate.py, 946 lines)
  • Paths: cache, runs dir, GCS prefixes from 3 env vars
  • Model catalog YAMLs under configs/pipeline/models
  • Dataset plans: fold plans, manifests, test-only patient lists

③ Run orchestration src/core

Decides which stages run, records what they produced, and moves runs to and from GCS.

  • Stage planner and resume: pipeline_runner.py
  • Run directory and manifest: v2_pipeline_run.py
  • Removal audit: Tracker shared across stages
  • Results store: publish, list, pull shared runs
  • Session tracking: training_session_tracker.py

④ Stage APIs src/core/stages

The stable contract. Each stage has Settings, settings_from_config, run_* and a Result.

  • preprocessing: load, cut, align, normalise, blip filter, overrides
  • clustering: valid/invalid per-breath aggregation
  • features: extraction, TSF, mRMR/pool selection, blind split
  • training: Monte-Carlo validation draws, threshold, test
  • holdout: patient-disjoint holdouts or k-fold OOF
  • visualization, model_reports

⑤ Algorithm modules src/core (≈40 files, flat)

The science. Grouped here by feature; on disk they sit in one folder.

  • Signal preparation: schema mapping, cutting, alignment, Gilad path vs GRID_CLEAN path, trigger detection, blips
  • Clustering: Single_signal_cluster.py
  • Feature engineering and selection: extraction (2.7k lines), poolsel, stability, labels
  • Training and evaluation: train.py (2.2k), partitions, folds, holdout results, explainability
  • Tuning: three near-identical Optuna tuners

⑥ Reporting src/visualization

Turns run artifacts into HTML/PNG reports.

  • Data reports: unit report, lab batch/day, lab feature window
  • Model reports: model_report.py (8,737 lines), SHAP, feature and patient scores
  • Partition report for the audit notebook
  • Heatmaps heat_vis.py: used only by legacy notebooks

⑦ Data and storage src/datasets, src/utils

Gets clinical data out of Cloud SQL into immutable GCS datasets and back into runs.

  • Extraction: per-site Cloud SQL queries
  • Dataset contract and manifest: columns, commit marker, checksums
  • GCS store: cache and download by dataset id
  • Legacy utils: gcs_utils, data_utils, model_utils, config.py

⑧ Model dashboard model_dashboard/

A separate deployable that reads published runs.

  • Builder: adapts run folders into a normalised bundle, optional DB blip enrichment
  • Service: Flask app on Cloud Run (2.7k lines in one file)
  • Build: cloudbuild.yaml, two Dockerfiles

⑨ Quality tests/, .cursor/rules

Guards the contracts.

  • Unit: 46 files, one per stage and most modules
  • Invariants: row conservation, split leakage, feature invariants
  • System: end-to-end pipeline
  • Team rules: 9 non-negotiables in pipeline-team-standards.mdc

Part 2

What to improve before the codebase grows

The stage layer is a good foundation: one config model, one set of stage APIs, tests per stage. The cost of growth sits below and around it. Items are ordered by how much they slow down the next feature. Every change below can keep old import paths alive with re-export shims, which keeps it within team rules 2, 4 and 8.

1

Group the flat src/core into feature packages

About 40 modules sit side by side, mixing the run framework (runner, run, tracker, results store) with science code (preprocessing, features, training, tuning). Nothing on disk tells a new person which files belong to which stage.

Target layout: core/run/, core/preprocessing/, core/clustering/, core/features/, core/training/, core/evaluation/ (holdout, partitions, folds), core/tuning/. Leave a one-line shim at each old path.

2

Make adding a stage a one-place change

Stages are wired by hand in STAGE_ORDER, STAGE_DEPENDENCIES, REQUIRED_ARTIFACTS, a special case in _dependencies, CLI subcommands, two notebook tiers and docs. The holdout stage shows the drift: it has a CLI command but no thin or full notebook, and the main docs do not mention it.

A small Stage protocol (name, depends_on, required_artifacts, settings_from_config, run) and a registry. The runner, the CLI and a notebook generator read the registry. A test fails when a registered stage has no notebook or doc section.

3

Split the oversized modules

model_report.py 8,737 lines, heat_vis.py 3,198, unit_report.py 3,062, feature_extraction.py 2,755, service/app.py 2,758, train.py 2,255. Files this size cause merge conflicts between the four or five people working on them and are hard to test piece by piece.

Split by section: for the model report, data loading, metrics tables, plots and HTML assembly. For feature extraction, one module per feature family behind a registry.

4

Fix the layer direction

src/visualization/model_report.py imports run internals (v2_pipeline_run, removal_audit) and legacy src/utils/data_utils, while stages import visualization. train.py still edits sys.path and falls back to from utils.model_utils.

Set one direction, config → datasets/io → algorithms → stages → interfaces, with reports reading only artifacts and the run manifest. Enforce it with import-linter in CI. Remove the sys.path hack.

5

Merge duplicated utilities and tuners

build_gcs_uri exists in both src/core/config/paths.py:73 and src/utils/gcs_utils.py:78. The three tuners, three tune scripts and three experiment YAMLs follow one pattern.

One GCS helper module. One generic tuner, with each model's search space in YAML and a single lucia_pipeline.py tune --model command.

6

Separate active code from dead or legacy code

Nothing in src/, scripts/ or active notebooks imports ensemble_decisions.py, feature_selection_stable.py or rebuild_prediction_tables.py. heat_vis.py and site_leading_features.py serve only frozen notebooks/gilad. eran_preprocess.py is reached only from tests. File names like Feature_Extraction_BB_June3_LUCIA.py do not follow PEP 8.

Confirm with each owner, then move to src/legacy/ or delete. Rename non-PEP 8 files with shims.

7

Turn one-off scripts into config

Four pin_* scripts each hard-code one dataset cut (for example pin_type2_batch1_drophuge2108ch17.py). The next cut means a fifth script.

One datasets pin --spec configs/datasets/<name>.yaml command. The YAML records which patients and channels are dropped and why.

8

Tidy configs, notebooks and dependencies

Experiments live in both configs/experiments/ and configs/pipeline/experiments/. Notebooks are organised by person, with .py scripts inside notebooks/gilad. Five requirements files and no pyproject.toml. Optuna is missing from the venv, so the tuning tests are skipped.

Configs by study (lucia550/, relive/, type1_61/). Notebooks by purpose (pipeline/, exploration/<topic>/, legacy/). A pyproject.toml with extras [pipeline], [tuning], [gpu], [dashboard] and a lock file.

9

Give the dashboard a written input contract

breath_v2_adapter.py (968 lines) reverse-engineers run folders. Team rule 2 forbids changing outputs, so the adapter is the only thing pinning the run layout.

Version the run manifest schema, have the dashboard read only the manifest, and add a contract test that builds a bundle from the e2e test run.

Part 3

What is in docs/

No document carries a version number, status or owner. The only versioning is git history, so the table uses it: the date a file was added, the date it last changed, how many commits touched it, and who changed it last.

Part 4

How documentation is done today

Works wellThe README points to a reading order. Guides are written for tasks and include real commands. Team rule 9 asks for docs in the same change. test_grid_clean_doc.py already checks a doc against code. The review tracker has a clear status vocabulary.
One flat folder, six kinds of documentGuides, reference, explanations, branch handoffs, a personal run log, a review tracker and slide decks sit together. A reader cannot tell which are maintained and which are snapshots.
No version, status or ownerNothing says which pipeline version or commit a doc describes, who owns it, or when it was last checked. Readers have to run git log to judge freshness.
Overlap causes driftThe 1,044-line architecture doc repeats the repo tree, config layers, run commands and failures that the user guide, quickstart and configuration reference also cover. When the holdout stage arrived, it went into a new file and none of the four core docs were updated.
Stale and contradictory factsNEW_VM_SETUP.md checks out lenny/new_pipe. Two docs point to gilad/PR38. The canonical-modules doc calls notebooks/gilad the production chain, while the README says it is frozen.
Inconsistent naming and binariesUPPER_CASE, lower_case and a filename with spaces. Two identical .pptx files. Slides are binary copies of Markdown docs and drift silently from them.
Part 5

Proposed documentation system

Sort every doc by the question it answers, using the four Diátaxis types, plus two folders for point-in-time records. Maintained docs describe the current code and are updated in the same PR. Records are dated, never edited after the fact, and are allowed to go stale.

docs/

├── CHANGELOG.md                  # pipeline versions; what changed for users
│

│   ├── runs/2026-11-05-relive-beta.md

Rules that keep it in order

  1. Front matter on every maintained doc: title, type, status (draft, current, superseded, archived), owner, last_reviewed, applies_to (pipeline version or commit). Records also carry date and branch.
  2. One home per fact. The repo tree lives in one reference page, config keys in one, commands in one. Other docs link and do not copy.
  3. Version the pipeline, not each doc. Tag releases (v2.1.0), write user-facing changes to CHANGELOG.md, and set applies_to on docs. Git keeps the history of each file.
  4. Naming: lowercase kebab-case, no spaces. Records start with an ISO date.
  5. Generate reference from code: config keys from the config model and validation_only.yaml, CLI help from argparse. A test fails when a config key or stage is not documented, extending what test_grid_clean_doc.py does today.
  6. CI checks: broken relative links, missing front matter, and a warning when last_reviewed is older than 90 days.
  7. PR template: one checkbox, "Docs updated or not needed", with the doc path.
  8. Slides are exports. Keep the Markdown as source, store decks on Drive, link them from the index.

Migration in three steps

  1. Quick fixes, one PR: delete the duplicate PR38.pptx, fix the branch names in NEW_VM_SETUP.md and the two gilad/PR38 notes, correct the production-chain line in the canonical-modules doc, add holdout to the README, user guide and configuration reference, and rename the file with spaces.

content.text:
I put the full report on one page: https://claude.ai/artifact/FhBeQ8kcaQJsZtG5wvBaVD (private until you share it from the page's Share menu).

**Structure.** The page has a block diagram of 8 main blocks, each listing its components by feature: interfaces, configuration, run orchestration, stage APIs, algorithm modules, reporting, data/storage, and the model dashboard. A ninth card covers tests and team rules. There is also a second diagram that follows one run through all 7 stages and the files each stage writes. In short: YAML config is resolved once, then the CLI and both notebook tiers call the same `src/core/stages/` functions. Those stages call about 40 algorithm modules that all sit in one flat folder.

**Top improvements before the codebase grows:**
1. **Group `src/core` into folders by feature** (run, preprocessing, features, training, evaluation, tuning). Leave a one-line file at each old path that re-exports the moved code, so existing imports keep working.
2. **Make adding a stage a one-place change.** Today a stage is wired by hand in `pipeline_runner.py:30`, the CLI, two notebook tiers and the docs. `holdout` already shows the drift: it has no notebook and is missing from the main docs.
3. **Split the very large files:** `model_report.py` (8,737 lines), `heat_vis`, `unit_report`, `feature_extraction`, `train`, and the dashboard `app.py`.
4. **Make dependencies point one way.** Report code imports run internals and old utilities, and `train.py` edits `sys.path` so it can import them. A lint rule in CI can enforce the direction.
5. **Merge duplicates:** two `build_gcs_uri` functions, three near-identical tuners, and four one-off `pin_*` dataset scripts. Move dead or legacy modules aside after checking with their owners.

**Docs.** The page has a table of all 22 files with their main content and kind. No doc has a version, status or owner, so I used git history as the version: date added, last change and author, and number of commits. The main problems:
- `PR38.pptx` and `download_dataset.pptx` are the same file.
- Some branch names are out of date: `NEW_VM_SETUP.md` still checks out `lenny/new_pipe`, and two docs point to `gilad/PR38`.
- The canonical-modules doc contradicts the README about whether `notebooks/gilad` is the production chain.
- The core guides don't mention `holdout`.
- The 1,044-line architecture doc overlaps three other docs.
- Handoff notes and a personal run log sit alongside maintained guides, with no way to tell them apart.

**Proposed system:** sort docs into `tutorials/`, `how-to/`, `reference/` and `explanation/` (the Diátaxis types), plus `decisions/` for decision records and `records/` for dated handoffs, experiments and reviews that never change after they're written. Each maintained doc gets a short header with status, owner, last-reviewed date and the pipeline version it describes. Version the pipeline with a `CHANGELOG.md` rather than versioning each doc. Generate the config and CLI references from code, and add CI checks for doc coverage and broken links. The page ends with a three-step migration plan; the first step is a quick-fix PR.

I only read code and git history for this and didn't change anything in the repo.

# Plan: understand the LUCIA codebase structure (v1)

Ticket: TBD (rename the file when a Jira ticket exists)
Date: 2026-11-19
Reference map: https://claude.ai/artifact/FhBeQ8kcaQJsZtG5wvBaVD (Part 1 only; Parts 2-5 are out of scope here)

## Scope

In scope: what the blocks are, how one run flows through them, where each kind of change belongs.
Out of scope: improving the code, reorganising docs, understanding each algorithm's math.

## Definition of Done (whole task)

The task is done when all of these are true:

1. You can draw the block diagram (interfaces, config, orchestration, stages, algorithms,
   reporting, data/storage, dashboard) from memory and name 2 key files in each block.
2. You can trace one run from YAML config to published results, naming the stage order
   and one artifact each stage writes.
3. You have run the pipeline yourself at least as a dry-run plus the end-to-end test,
   and found the run directory it produced.
4. You can say where these 3 changes would go: a new config key, a new feature
   in feature extraction, a new stage.
5. You can tell active code from legacy/personal code by folder.
6. You answer at least 8 of the 10 check questions at the bottom without looking.
7. You have written a 1-page summary in your own words
   (`.claude.local/notes/codebase-summary.md`).

## Sub-tasks

Do them in order. Each one builds on the previous.

### S1. Big picture
Read: `README.md`, `docs/PIPELINE_V2_USER_GUIDE.md` sections "What the pipeline does"
and "Repository map", `.cursor/rules/pipeline-team-standards.mdc`.

Done when:
- [ ] You can say in 3 sentences what the pipeline does.
- [ ] You can name the 3 interfaces (CLI, thin notebooks, full notebooks) and the folder
      they all call (`src/core/stages/`).
- [ ] You can state the gist of the 9 team rules, one line each.

### S2. Run it
Read: `docs/PIPELINE_V2_QUICKSTART.md` sections 1-2.
Do: activate the venv, run
`python scripts/lucia_pipeline.py run --config configs/pipeline/example_run_lucia.yaml --dry-run`,
then `pytest tests/system tests/unit -q`.

Done when:
- [ ] The dry-run prints a stage plan and you can read it.
- [ ] Tests run; you have written down pass/skip counts and why tests were skipped.
- [ ] You found where local runs are written (`LUCIA_RUNS_DIR`, default `~/lucia-runs`).

### S3. Configuration
Read: `src/core/config/` (`loader.py`, `merge.py`, `model.py`), `configs/pipeline/validation_only.yaml`,
`configs/pipeline/example_run_lucia.yaml`, `docs/pipeline_v2_configuration.md` "Configuration layers".

Done when:
- [ ] You can explain the 3 config layers and which one wins.
- [ ] You traced one key (e.g. `features.n_features`) from YAML to the line of stage code that reads it.
- [ ] You can name the 3 allowed environment variables.

### S4. Orchestration
Read: `src/core/pipeline_runner.py` (top constants, `resolve_stage_plan`, `should_skip_stage`,
`run_pipeline`), `src/core/v2_pipeline_run.py` (`PipelineRun`, `record_artifact`),
`Tracker` in `src/core/removal_audit.py`.

Done when:
- [ ] You can draw the stage dependency graph (7 stages).
- [ ] You can explain how a run is resumed and when a stage is skipped.
- [ ] You can say what the run manifest and the Tracker record.

### S5. Stages, one at a time
Read: each file in `src/core/stages/` and the algorithm module it calls.
Do it in 4 sittings: (a) preprocessing + clustering, (b) features, (c) training + holdout,
(d) visualization + model_reports.

Done when:
- [ ] You filled this table for all 7 stages:

  | Stage | Reads | Calls (algorithm module) | Writes | Key config section |
  |---|---|---|---|---|

- [ ] You can explain the difference between the `training` and `holdout` stages.
- [ ] You know which stage enforces patient-level separation (and why it matters, rule 7).

### S6. Data in and out
Read: `docs/shared_datasets.md`, `src/datasets/__init__.py`, `src/core/results_store.py`,
`model_dashboard/README.md`.

Done when:
- [ ] You can draw the path Cloud SQL -> published dataset -> local cache -> run dir
      -> GCS results -> dashboard bundle.
- [ ] You know the 3 top-level GCS folders (`datasets/`, `results/`, `models/`) and what goes in each.
- [ ] You can run `python scripts/lucia_pipeline.py runs list` (or know why you cannot: GCS access).

### S7. Active vs legacy
Read: `docs/NOTEBOOK_MIGRATION.md`, folder listing of `notebooks/`, `scripts/`, `src/utils/`.

Done when:
- [ ] Every top-level folder and `notebooks/` subfolder is labelled active, legacy or personal.
- [ ] You know which folders must not be used for new work (`notebooks/gilad/`, any `archive/`).

### S8. Wrap-up
Do: close all files, draw the block diagram on paper, answer the check questions,
write the 1-page summary.

Done when:
- [ ] Whole-task DoD items 1, 4, 6 and 7 are met.
- [ ] Open questions you still have are listed at the end of the summary.

## Check questions

1. Which file decides the stage order and dependencies?
2. Which 3 files must preprocessing leave for the stage to count as complete?
3. In which order are config layers applied?
4. Which stage functions do the CLI and notebooks call, and from which package?
5. What is the difference between thin and full notebooks?
6. What does the `holdout` stage do that `training` does not?
7. Where in GCS do published run results go?
8. What does the `Tracker` record, and why is it shared across stages?
9. Which folders are frozen legacy and must not be used for new work?
10. A new config knob is needed. What must it have, according to team rule 4?

## Answer key (check only after answering)

1. `src/core/pipeline_runner.py` (`STAGE_ORDER`, `STAGE_DEPENDENCIES`).
2. `processed.pkl`, `tracker.pkl`, `section_landmarks.json`.
3. `validation_only.yaml` -> run YAML -> CLI `--set` overrides (last wins).
4. `run_*` functions from `src/core/stages/`.
5. Same stage APIs; full notebooks add read-only diagnostics, no second algorithm.
6. Several patient-disjoint holdouts (or k-fold), feature selection inside each holdout,
   pooled test predictions per patient.
7. `gs://nanose_ml/datasets_models/lucia/results/<dataset>/<selection>/<owner>/<experiment>/<run-id>/`.
8. Rows removed at each step and why; later stages read it (e.g. features reads clustering settings).
9. `notebooks/gilad/` and any `archive/` folder (e.g. `notebooks/lenny/archive/`).
10. A safe default that keeps current behaviour for existing configs.
